payload.title: Park uncommitted main changes and file tasks to land them
payload.description: Park the uncommitted changes on main onto a temp branch, work out why each change was made, group them into tasks, then work and land those tasks until main is clean.
payload.plan:
# Plan: Park uncommitted main changes and file tasks to land them

The main checkout of go-testutil has uncommitted work that predates this task. Other repos may build against that working tree through local `replace` directives. The goal is a clean main, with every change either landed through a task or deliberately dropped by the maintainer.

The changes at filing time (2026-10-19), excluding `.endless/`:

- Modified: go.mod, go.sum, examples/basic_usage/go.mod, examples/basic_usage/go.sum, test/go.mod, test/go.sum.
- This looks like one dependency change: go.mod bumps go-dt from v0.3.3 to v0.5.0 and adds local `replace` directives for go-cliutil, go-dt and go-dt/dtx, so the WIP builds against those siblings' own uncommitted main working trees. Those replaces are why this task waits on theirs.
- go-cfgstore's test module requires go-testutil v0.3.0, which is not tagged yet, and reaches it through a local replace.

## Steps

1. **Snapshot without touching main.** From this task's worktree, read the main checkout's full diff against HEAD, staged and unstaged together, including deletions, binaries and untracked non-`.endless/` files. Recreate it on a branch named `wip/<task-id>` cut from main's HEAD, and commit it there as one commit with message "WIP snapshot of main working tree". Then confirm the branch's tree matches main's working tree file for file. Don't use `git stash`; the stash stack is shared across sessions.
2. **Analyze.** Go through the snapshot and work out why each change was made, from the code, nearby commits and other repos that depend on it. Group the changes into coherent units. Flag anything that looks unfinished, accidental, or like a generated artifact.
3. **Report to the user before filing.** Show the grouping, what each group is for, and anything you couldn't explain, then let them adjust it.
4. **File one task per agreed group** in this project. Each plan names the files and hunks it takes from `wip/<task-id>`.
5. **Check whether dependents rely on the WIP.** Find sibling repos whose go.mod has a `replace` pointing at this checkout. Build each one against this repo at main HEAD, without the WIP, using a scratch GOWORK that points this module at a clean checkout. Add blockers for whatever fails: each group whose removal breaks the build gets `--blocks` on the tasks that need it.
6. **Hand the user one command to clear main's working tree.** They run it themselves, only after confirming `wip/<task-id>` holds everything. This session doesn't write to the main checkout.

## Done when

Every change in the snapshot belongs to a filed task or is listed as "drop" with the user's agreement, main is clean, and any build dependency is recorded as a blocker.

payload.title: Raise go.mod files to Go 1.27 via gomion repo setup
payload.description: Raise every go.mod in go-testutil to Go 1.27 by running gomion repo setup once the in-flight go.mod/go.sum changes are committed
payload.context:
Gomion task E-2454 is adding `gomion repo setup`, which (among other steps) raises every module's `go` directive to Go 1.27 and tidies. Go 1.27 is now the minimum for Mike's go-pkgs repos because json/v2 no longer needs GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2 there. Generated CI pins Go 1.27 and no longer sets GOEXPERIMENT.

When E-2454 ran, go-testutil's working tree held uncommitted changes from this project's own in-flight work in: go.mod, go.sum, test/go.mod, test/go.sum, examples/basic_usage/go.mod, examples/basic_usage/go.sum. On 2026-10-28 Mike chose to let this project's own tasks handle their own changes rather than have E-2454 commit around them. So E-2454 committed only the regenerated .github/workflows files here and left every go.mod in go-testutil alone. `gomion repo setup --check` reports go-testutil's modules as below Go 1.27 until this task runs.

fields.title: Adopt gomion's generated CI and Release workflows
fields.description: Adopt gomion's generated CI and Release workflows in go-testutil by running gomion repo setup, committing the result, and confirming the first Actions runs show no warnings or notices
fields.plan:
# Plan: adopt gomion's generated workflows in go-testutil

0. Commit or finish the in-flight go.mod/go.sum changes first. `gomion repo setup` refuses a module whose go.mod or go.sum has uncommitted changes, and reports it as refused.
1. Use a gomion build that includes E-2454's `gomion repo` commands.
2. In go-testutil, run `gomion repo setup`. It raises each go.mod below Go 1.27 and tidies it, then writes .github/workflows/test.yml and release.yml.
3. Run `gomion repo setup --check`; it must report the repo up to date.
4. Run each module's tests locally with GOWORK=off.
5. Commit the generated workflows and the raised go.mod/go.sum files together.

After the land: push, then read the annotations on the first Test run (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/check-runs/<job id>/annotations` for each job), and on the next Release run once there is one. Each must show zero warnings and zero notices; any that remain are fixed in gomion's templates, not here.

payload.title: Prepare go-testutil for a tagged release
payload.description: Prepare go-testutil for release by committing and pushing pending work, then propose a version and description per module for the owner to tag.
payload.plan:
## Plan
1. Run `git status` and `git log <latest-tag>..HEAD` in the go-testutil repo; list every module in it that has its own go.mod and tag prefix.
2. Commit any uncommitted work that belongs in the release. Ask the owner about anything unclear instead of guessing.
3. Run the repo's build, vet and tests. Fix or report any failure.
4. Push main to origin. Do not create or push tags.
5. For each module, compare the changes since its latest tag and propose a semver version, explaining whether the change is breaking.
6. Draft a release description for each module.
7. Report the proposed versions and descriptions to the owner. The owner tags and releases when ready.

fields.outcome:
## Release proposal for go-testutil

go-testutil has one versioned module, the root `github.com/mikeschinkel/go-testutil`. The `test/` and `examples/basic_usage/` modules are unversioned helpers with a `replace` to the root and are never tagged.

**Last tag:** v0.2.1 (2025-12-01, commit 6ce0e95).

**Changes since v0.2.1, outside .endless/:**

- Breaking: six `BufferedWriter` accessors are renamed to say what they capture. `GetStdout` → `GetPrintOutput`, `GetStderr` → `GetErrorOutput`, `GetStdoutLines` → `GetPrintLines`, `GetStderrLines` → `GetErrorLines`, `CountStdoutLines` → `CountPrintLines`, `CountStderrLines` → `CountErrorLines`. `ContainsStdout`, `ContainsStderr`, `ContainsOutput`, `GetAllOutput` and `Reset` keep their names. Callers of the old names fail to compile.
- Dependencies: go-cliutil v0.2.0 → v0.4.0 and go-dt v0.2.6 → v0.6.1 (go-dt/appinfo v0.3.0 and go-dt/dtx v0.2.2 indirect). Consumers pick up the newer siblings transitively.
- Toolchain: `go 1.27.0` in every go.mod. A consumer on an older toolchain upgrades through GOTOOLCHAIN or by hand.
- Build and CI: golangci-lint pinned at v2.15.0; both workflows on Go 1.27 with GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2 dropped; release notes exclude commits that touch only .endless/; /bin/ gitignored.

**Proposed version: v0.3.0.** The accessor rename is a breaking API change, and under v0.x semver a breaking change bumps the minor. go-cliutil/test and go-cfgstore/test already require go-testutil v0.3.0 behind a local replace, so this is the version those modules expect.

**Draft release description** (the `description` input of the Release workflow):

> Renames BufferedWriter's accessors to say what they capture: GetPrintOutput, GetErrorOutput, GetPrintLines, GetErrorLines, CountPrintLines and CountErrorLines replace GetStdout, GetStderr, GetStdoutLines, GetStderrLines, CountStdoutLines and CountStderrLines; callers of the old names must update. Requires go-cliutil v0.4.0, go-dt v0.6.1 and Go 1.27.

**Order of operations for the owner:** land E-2511, push main, run the Release workflow with version `v0.3.0` and the description above. gomion can then drop its replace for go-testutil and require v0.3.0.
